Plain Content: As you will know, Rotherfield FC is now a 2 Star England Football Accredited Club.  We are one of only 47 clubs across the whole of Sussex with 2 Star status. In addition there are only 3 clubs within Sussex with the top accolade of 3 Stars. As a consequence of our 2 Star status we will receive support from the Sussex County FA Thriving Community Club Liaison Manager to discuss the resources available to us from the FA & SCFA to help sustain & develop our club. We will also receive support from an FA Club consultant to further help us plan our future. Before all this occurs we should decide what we want! We are looking for people in our club to form a working group to ensure all aspects of our club are equally reviewed to identify the improvements we would like to make. This will then be the framework for discussions with the FA/SCFA to arrive at our Future plan. Issues such as pitch condition, pitch availability, Committee structures, Junior club, Girls football, open age adult football, Veterans football, Women’s football, Disability football pathway, club house facilities, grounds machinery/maintenance, support for coaches, support for administrators & succession planning for our key (but ageing!) people all need to be considered.  Please consider if you would like to be part of this exciting planning for the future. We are looking for people in our club to form a working group to ensure all aspects of our club are equally reviewed to identify the improvements we would like to make. This will then be the framework for discussions with the FA/SCFA to arrive at our Future plan. Our club has been around since 1893 & we doubt that the founding individuals ever thought the club would have well over 400 members participating in football as we do today. Where will the club be in 5, 10 or even 25 years?  This is your chance to shape our future. If you would like to help develop the future of your club, then please register your interest by contacting us by Wednesday 30th April on enquiriesrfc1893@gmail.com

Rotherfield FC send Bill's family their condolences at this time.

Plain Content: With seven weeks without a game and then a late venue change, Rotherfield travelled to The Colwell Ground in Haywards Heath to face Lindfield. It was clear the challenging surface was not going to aid a fluid passing contest and there were a number of occasions when players had the ball stuck under their feet or slipped. Despite this, both sides still tried to play to feet and Rotherfield in particular had success with combinations to get the ball forward. It was the hosts the opened the scoring where Grant Reed manged to evade a number of defenders in the box and slot home past Sumner. 0-1 down at the break was not a massive issue as Rotherfield looked threating at times going forwards. Soon into the second half Jack Spampanato managed to beat the offside trap and was through one-on-one with the Keeper which he dispatched his final ball with aplomb. However, a great delivery from Lindfield's Stuart Brown, with about twenty minutes remaining found the head of the Andrew Davies to make it 2-1. Rotherfield had a number opportunities to make it 2-2 and the introduction of debutants Cameron Howard and Bailey Mintrim certainly provided a positive threat going forwards, but Lindfield stood firm and denied the Greens (in Yellow) a share of the spoils. Final Score 2-1.

Plain Content: Image: Will Hugall Wayne Clarke's Rotherfield side were involved in a game of two halves on Saturday as they entertained Balcombe. More changes were required, with a number of injuries and availability issues, the back four had to have another reshuffle, with John Sinclair and Calum Ridley filling in at centre back and James Dunn at right back. The unfamiliarity of players not in their usual positions may have contributed to the opening goal. The Greens were on the back foot early on as Balcombe had a throw-in inside the Rotherfield final third. The ball was launched into the box and the defensive set up were unable to deal with the throw in effectively and the ball ended up in the net on their opening salvo. 5 minutes in and 0-1 down. Only a couple of minutes after the restart, a scramble for the ball inside the Greens half was won by the visitors and allowed the Balcombe forward to advance towards the Rotherfield goal. He hit a shot which sailed over James Gurney to make it 0-2. Despite the 2 goal deficit, Rotherfield didn't panic and were patient out of possession, allowing the visitors to keep the ball in their own half and try an steal it as they approached the halfway line. The Greens emerged from the half time break with a clear intention and it was only three minutes after the whistle that the game turned when Jack Spampanato hit a wonderful strike from range to make it 1-2. 10 minutes into the second half, Connor Morrow, drove down the left flank and sent a diagonal ball to his opposite flank which Dan Gray managed to get a cross in for Ross Treleaven to head home. Both sides had opportunities to score more but good goalkeeping, solid defending and wasteful chances prevented the score to change. Most notably Sean Bristow tried a long range lob, which the Balcombe keeper got a hand to and Dan Gray was also denied by the keeper right at the death when his effort was saved. A good point against a usual strong Balcombe side. Final score 2-2. Team: Gurney, Dunn, Sinclair, Ridley, Kerslake, Saunders, Peevor, Spampanato, Kent, Treleaven, Morrow. Subs: Gray, Bristow, Ridley. A sharp shower prior to kick-off made the surface quick and the ball was zipping around the pitch and as the contest settled, there was few goal opportunities.  Ross Treleaven came close with an effort that was parried away by Westfield's keeper.  But with five minutes remaining of the half, Patteson Riugaimae put the Westies in front to take them into the break with the lead.  The second half was a disastrous start with Micheal Rwabigwi doubling the visitors lead within the 10 minutes of the restart. Just past the hour mark and Dan Tewksbury was able to make it three, then moments from full time, Josh Pickering made it four. A hard day on the pitch, but Rotherfield did come close to scoring with Connor Morrow having an effort hit the side netting, and Dan Gray hitting an effort which would have been goal of the season if the crossbar was a couple of inches higher. Squad: Davies, Russell, Carbune, Ridley, Kent, Sinclair, Saunders, Peevor, Spampanato, Treleaven, Morrow Subs: Fyffe, Gray, Kerslake, Teague, Watts (unused) Man Of The Match: Archie Russell - probably his best performance to date, being strong defensively and not allowing either Westfield wingers any joy.

Plain Content: IMAGE: WILL HUGALL Rotherfield welcomed league flyers Frenches Athletic on Saturday. With a very strong squad, the Greens stood up to the task of facing a side to have only lost one game so far. The hosts got off to a perfect start making use of Ross Treleaven's missile throw in, deep into the Frenches half. With just 2 minutes gone, debutant George Fyffe flicks his header over the Frenches keeper and in the bottom far corner. Frenches Athletic did almost come back with a reply soon after when a Frenches forward manged to get through the Rotherfield lines and get a shot away, but keeper Rob Davies was equal to it by saving to his left and getting the ball to clip the post and go wide. Twenty fives minutes in, a touch of déjà vu happened. A throw in was awarded in a similar position to the previous. Treleaven wound up another long throw which torpedoed beyond the far post for Sinclair to head across goal and for Jack Turner to nod in to double the lead. The remainder of the half, Rotherfield rode out the the storm, with numbers behind the ball and being marshalled well by Turner, Ridley, and skipper Saunders. Despite Frenches dominance in possession, they produced little threat at goal. The second half started as the first half ended with the visitors having lots of the ball. Just past the hour mark, Frenches halved the deficit with good approach play and a good finish into the bottom corner. Quarter of an hour later, half time substitute George Boynton scored to make it 3-1 and scoring in two consecutive fixtures. Frenches did get a second from the penalty mark as Rob Davies brought down the advancing forward in the box. But with five minutes of normal time remaining, Dan Gray secures Rotherfield's third win in a row by clipping a ball over the keeper to make the final score 4-2. Squad: Davies, Russell, Turner, Ridley, Kent, Sinclair, Saunders, Peevor, Spampanato, Fyffe, Treleaven. Subs: Boynton, Dunn, Gray, Kerslake, Watts (unused).

Who To Watch Alex Pollard was a prolific goal scorer last season, finding the net on 30 occasions in 31 appearances. He has continued his good form so far scoring 4 goals in three games alongside Tom Hawkins who equals Pollard's tally. Plain Content: A few weeks ago we posted a set of questions to establish how well you know our club. These are the answers! Please review to improve your understanding. Ensure you share relevant information with your child. It will only help their development! What is England Football Accredited? - England Football Accredited is for all non-professional leagues and clubs. It helps them create the experiences and environments where players, coaches and volunteers can thrive. Accredited clubs are more sustainable, more resilient and built to last. What EFA star rating is Rotherfield FC? 2 stars Rotherfield is an FA accredited Wildcats centre. What is Wildcats? Informal football for girls of primary school age. What format (in terms of number of players per side) do u8 teams play in the CDJFL? 5v5 What format do our u12 team play? 9v9 What size football is used in u10 mini soccer? Size 3 What do you understand by the term Powerplay in respect of junior football? Rule for junior football teams where a team is losing by a 4 goal margin, then the losing team can bring on an extra player to improve competitiveness.  How many minutes are played in a half of CDJFL u9 mini soccer? Depends on how many matches are played on a matchday. U9s have a maximum of 60 minutes playing time per day. If there's only one match then it can be 30 minute halves, however it is recommended that age group play 50 minutes per day to avoid overexertion. RJFC usually have 10-15 minute halves as we typically have 2 matches on a match day. What are the dimensions of a correct (in accordance with FA guidelines) set of goals in u13 football? 21 feet wide x 7 feet high  What do you understand by the term “rolling substitutes” in respect of football? Unlimited substitutions, players can be rolled on and off throughout the matches When can a referee sin bin a player in junior football? When a player is deemed to have shown dissent towards a match official. What colour of card is used to denote a sin bin? Yellow What is the duration of a sin bin? 8 minutes in matches under 90 minutes, 10 minutes in any 90 minute match Why do players wear shin pads? This a mandatory piece of equipment, to protect a players shin. The shin extends from the top of the ankle to just below the knee  What do you understand by a “silent weekend”? This is a weekend where spectators and coaches are encouraged to only applaud good play and refrain from shouting instructions. Why are silent weekends important? To allow players to be able to focus, communicate and make their own decisions without parents (& others) incessantly shouting confusing instructions! What does a yellow arm band signify when worn by a referee? Referee is under 18. Recognise this & give the young referee respect. What is the purpose of marked Technical areas in mini soccer? Area for coaches and game changers (substitutes) so match officials know participants in the tech area are game changers or coaches. Coaches & game changers to remain within the technical areas & not prowl up & down the touchline. The game is for the children. What is the purpose of a Respect barrier in junior football? To allow space for players, keeping spectators back from the touchline. Please always stand behind the barrier!

After lots of work on the pitch during the week the surface should be excellent (weather permitting) & the players should be confident after a very good performance last week albeit in a narrow defeat. Room for improvement! The side is virtually unchanged & the management team are looking forward to further progression from the likes of Cameron Routledge, Archie Russel, Ethan Laughton-Zimmerman & especially George Fyffe following their levels of last week. Training this week had a real buzz of quality with infectious displays from Peevor & Teague from the more experienced players & equally influential performances from Jacob & Jasper at the other end of the age range! Fixture: Rotherfield vs Cuckfield Rangers Venue: Rotherfield Recreation Ground, North Street, TN6 3LX Kick Off: 2pm Referee: Nick Greenfield Half-Time refreshments available, bar open after Full Time. Plain Content: Young Greens exit the Stratford Cup on Penalties in a closely-fought encounter against Crawley United. This would be the first Home game for the Rotherfield side since September, with the greens stringing together a series of stubborn away performances culminating in back-to-back wins against Willingdon and Ringmer in recent weeks. The confident Rotherfield side started the brighter, playing the ball across the back with composure against an aggressive press without creating anything of note in the early stages.  Captain Ridley setting the tone alongside the returning King and ever-reliable Sutton. Crawley then pegged the greens into their own half with their high press rattling the previously-composed backline and preventing Rotherfield from playing out. Unable to link with the influential midfield pairing of Birdsall and Chittenden, the ball ended up being thrust forward long and early to strikers Bowen and Blackstone, playing straight into the hands of the powerful Crawley rearguard and putting Rotherfield further onto the back foot. A series of Crawley corners caused by long, raking balls into the channels created chaos in the Rotherfield penalty-area, with only the lightning reflexes of Gurney keeping the greens level. Rotherfield then settled down and looked to impose themselves physically on the game, limiting the away side to longer efforts that whistled over the bar, with fullback Holman working hard to win the ball back down the Rotherfield right and releasing the young and lively Caird on the break. It was now the turn of the home side to swing the ball into the Crawley penalty-area, with a series of corners and long throws from the left, and efforts from Lelliot and Birdsall from outside the box being the closest the greens had come so far. The final-third quality was lacking from both sides throughout the first half, so fair to say the teams had resigned themselves to going into the break at 0-0.  However, a poorly-pressed thrown-in down the greens left resulted in a scuffed cross that eluded several outstretched Rotherfield legs, leaving Gurney helpless and the Crawley forward the easiest of finishes.  The ball barely had time to make it back to the centre circle before the whistle blew for half-time - making the goal even more disappointing for the home side. After being set some challenges at halftime by Manager Bowen, the greens once again started the brighter, with some aggressive midfield play from Birdsall and Chittenden, along with the willing-running of Blackstone setting the tone early on.  Again, the away side dealt with the early green pressure with ease and regained control of the game. Technical midfield play putting the Rotherfield fullbacks into races down the channels, and requiring the very best of stopper Gurney to keep the young home side in the game. As with the previous week against Ringmer, the changes proved to be the difference again, with the introduction of the pacey Brazier and the trickery of McInulty on the flanks causing immediate chaos on the Crawley backline.  A high-press from Brazier resulted in a ricocheted ball landing at the feet of McInulty, who glided past several members of the Crawley defence before slipping the ball to the lively Blackstone who finished from close range at the 2nd time of asking after a good initial save from the Crawley keeper. Further substitutions were made by the Rotherfield management team (1 manager with no voice, and 5 subs acting as a megaphone), with young Thomas, tall Evans  and energetic Furman entering the fray late in the game to provide some fresh impetus. The game briefly levelled-off after the Rotherfield equaliser, before the away side once again dominated the centre of the pitch and created several gilt-edged chances to win the tie and save the game from the gloomy penalty shootout that had started to look inevitable.  Green stopper Gurney stood tall and alone in the face of several goal-bound efforts, with a number of saves leaving the away bench in disbelief and utter-contempt toward the young keeper. Manager Bowen managed to sneak in a few further substitutions in lieu of the impending shootout, with Player Bowen and Blackstone returning to defend a final corner before the whistle blew for full-time. The greens were full of confidence going into the lottery of penalties, with an in-form keeper and half the squad immediately volunteering to take the long, lonely walk to the spot.  The lack of final-third quality in open play had been replaced after the full-time whistle with 10 excellently-struck penalties from both sides - taking this nervy event into sudden death.  The high-quality shootout continued, with only a top save from the Crawley stopper able to swing the tie in the away-side’s favour - followed by another strong Crawley penalty to end the tie and knock the greens out of the Stratford Cup. On reflection, probably a fair result given the balance of play with green’s keeper Gurney receiving the plaudits from both sides, and the subsequent Man of the Match award. Nevertheless, the young Rotherfield side, and their 2nd half performance, help retain their upward momentum as they return to league duties away against an even-younger Brighton & Sussex Medical School side next week, who will be looking to get revenge after a 5-1 defeat early on in the season.

Firstly, Elliot Ridley-Smith was the recipient of the Club Assistant Referee of the Season award. This is the third win for Elliot & is recognition from referees throughout the season as to his excellence. Our Reserves were runners up in the Sportsmanship trophy, for all 115 teams in the league, only very narrowly pipped at the post! This shows that the success achieved during last season is possible without compromising behaviour. Finally the Reserves were the clear winners of the Division 3S merit table. This reflects on field achievements, referee marks for sportmanship & off field team administration. Again a fantastic achievement. The club won £150 for this win from the generous sponsorship of the league by Gray Hooper Holt LLP.

Plain Content: Rotherfield FC have now completed their fourth week of pre-season training at Rotherfield Recreation Ground. Despite the recent arid weather leaving the grass areas extremely hard and much of the grass having died off, the squad have continued to put in the hard work, making use of every available area to ensure each session has gone ahead. The commitment from the players has been outstanding, with more than 30 players regularly attending training each week. The excellent turnout has created a competitive environment, with players pushing each other as preparations continue for the new campaign. The squad have also played three pre-season friendlies, giving everyone the opportunity to build match fitness, gain valuable minutes on the pitch and impress the management team ahead of the season. With pre-season progressing well, the focus now turns to being ready for our first league fixture of the season on Saturday 22nd August. The hard work continues, and we look forward to seeing everyone back at Rotherfield Recreation Ground as the countdown to the new season goes on.

Plain Content: Gray Hooper Holt LLP Mid Sussex Football League Premier Division Venue: The Hybrid Fitness Stadium (home of Merstham FC) Rotherfield extended their unbeaten run to three matches—and an impressive 270 minutes without conceding—with a hard-fought goalless draw against Frenches Athletic in what was their fourth consecutive away fixture. The contest proved to be an evenly matched affair, particularly in a quiet first half where clear-cut chances were at a premium. Frenches Athletic came closest to opening the scoring midway through the half, seeing a flurry of efforts blocked before a final deflected shot fell safely into the hands of James Gurney. Rotherfield’s best opportunity of the opening period arrived ten minutes later. Sam Saunders picked up possession around 20 yards from goal and struck a powerful effort that fizzed narrowly wide, offering a glimpse of attacking intent in an otherwise subdued half. Aside from a handful of speculative attempts from both sides, neither goalkeeper was seriously tested before the break. The second half followed a similar pattern, though Rotherfield began to grow into the game as it progressed. Just after the hour mark, Saunders had another chance from a free kick in a dangerous position, but his effort sailed over the bar. Moments later, Rotherfield carved out arguably their best opening of the match. Connor Morrow won possession high up the pitch and drove forward before unleashing a shot from distance. The Frenches goalkeeper could only parry into the path of Scott Taylor, but he was unable to capitalise, firing over from a promising position. As the game wore on, Rotherfield started to assert more control, applying pressure on the Frenches back line. Max Carbune delivered a long diagonal free kick from deep inside his own half, with Morrow again getting on the end of it, but his header drifted over. With 15 minutes remaining, returning midfielder John Sinclair created an impactful moment, picking up the ball in the centre of the park and releasing Taylor who was further forward, Taylor’s pass allowed Morrow another sight of goal, but his effort rolled just wide of the post. The closing stages became a battle of resilience, with Rotherfield’s defensive unit—Carbune, Turner, Ridley, Kerslake, and goalkeeper Gurney—standing firm against anything the hosts could muster. However, despite their late dominance, Rotherfield were unable to find a breakthrough. In the end, both sides had to settle for a point. While the result maintains Rotherfield’s unbeaten run and defensive solidity, there may be a sense that the Greens could have done more to claim all three points.

Photo credit: Andrew Hazelden This week our First Team welcome Bosham FC in the Sussex County FC Intermediate Challenge Cup 1st round.  Bosham are based west of Chichester so we hope they have a safe journey up to the Recreation Ground. The Robins compete in Division 2 of the Southern Combination League. Last Time Out Bosham played away to Southwater last week in a difficult contest for them. Bosham lost 0-8.  Previous Meeting Rotherfield played Bosham in the same competition back in February 2023. The Greens had a scratch side and were made to bow out of the competition losing 4-1. John Penny netting for the Greens as stand in striker. Despite the defeat, Rotherfield received a very warm welcome and were looked after very well. Fixture Details Rotherfield vs Bosham FC Venue: Rotherfield Recreation Ground, TN6 3LX  Kick off: 2pm Referee: John Elms Halftime refreshments available. Bar open after match. Plain Content: As November started with early morning heavy rain to hasten in Winter, the Reserves were pleased to travel for the sixth consecutive week (irony)! On arrival at Barcombe they were greeted by a pitch with really long grass & a slope better suited to crampons than studs! With manager James Bowen needing to assume a new player-manager role, the warm up was taken by new Reserves coach Ollie “Slot” Caird. Well at least the hair style is similar. Playing up the mountain into the teeth of a Himalayan breeze, Rotherfield started the first half really well. Patience on the ball, passing to feet & with decent offensive movement created a number of half chances but powder puff finishing wasted these opportunities. Defensively the Greens were excellent with organisation & distances to the fore. The loss of Craig King with a groin strain after 20 minutes meant a reshuffle. Rich Holman dropped into right back, the fast lane given the skill level of the young Barcombe winger, & Jonah Caird came off the bench, fresh from his exploration of all things Italian for the last 3 months! Hopefully all things! Barcombe opened the scoring with the source from the dangerous left flank, but a wicked deflection was instrumental in the ball finding the net. Then just before half time a cross from the right was horribly miss-judged by keeper Rob who ultimately punched the ball into his own net. Rushing down the mountain in the second half saw Rotherfield give every ounce of energy & to their credit they still tried to build up from the back. From a really well delivered in swinging corner by Will Sutton (one of a number in the second half) a volley from skipper Owen Ridley smashed against the bar. However as Barcombe exploited the space by stretching the game on both flanks with their wide players hogging the touchlines (please note any opposition managers) a third goal arrived again conceived from wide left. The final finish was powerful & in the corner oozing quality. A fourth goal for the home side came when once again the wide left player jinked past three before shooting into the roof of the net from 20 yards. Then with a change of tactic the visitors went long from keeper Davies & when Connor Evans was first to the ball his lob over the advancing keeper was just wide. The legs of the midfield players tired as recovery runs up the mountain became difficult even for Jack “the GOAT” Birdsall. More Toggenberg than the greatest of all time, he never gave up & kept trying to drive the team forward, whilst at the back player-manager Bowen continually showed he was class (albeit middle rather than landed gentry). Then as the game approached the final throes the heavens opened with a torrential down pour. Monsoon season in the Himalayas! Not very pleasant for the partisans who were watching. The home side deserved their comfortable victory but there were plenty of positives for the visitors, a point made very succinctly with erudition by James “Downton” Bowen. Squad: Davies, King, Ridley O, Bowen J, Sutton, Bristow, Birdsall, Holman, Brazier, Ridley B, Bowen L. Subs used: Caird, Chittenden, Furman, Evans

Plain Content: Preparations for the new season at Rotherfield Football Club are edging ever closer with the club’s full senior pre-season programme being announced. Sessions start up once again on Tuesday the 30th of June at the Rotherfield Recreation Ground from 18:00-20:00 with sessions running twice a week, every Tuesday and Thursday, until the season starts.   The first week of sessions, Tuesday the 30th of June and Thursday 2nd July, will see the club hold two open training sessions where all prospective new players are invited to attend alongside the club’s existing players. This will afford prospective new players the opportunity to sample the club and impress the side’s management. All prospective new players wishing to join the first week’s open training sessions are advised to contact First Team Manager, Wayne Clarke, on 07540 765685.   All pre-season sessions will be led by the First Team Management Team, Wayne Clarke and Callum Ridley, with other qualified club coaches supporting the sessions too. Training will be supported by the First Team’s announced pre-season friendly programme that sees six fixtures taking place before the season starts proper. The club’s Reserve Team pre-season fixtures, now being led by Richard Holman, are in the final stages of being agreed and will be announced shortly.   The 2026/27 campaign looks set to be a strong one for all Rotherfield FC members with all three senior sides, Firsts, Reserves and Veterans, buoyed by excellent finishes to the previous campaign.   We look forward to seeing as many of you as possible from Tuesday the 30th of June as possible!

Plain Content: Today Rotherfield Football Club are delighted to announce the appointment of new First Team Head Coach Wayne Clarke. Chairman Peter Ford stated: I am delighted to advise that Wayne will take up the role of first team head coach -with immediate effect in time to orchestrate pre-season preparations that commence on 2nd July. Wayne is well known in local football having been an extremely successful player in FA level 4 & 5 clubs, making the game look ludicrously easy! However it was his passion for football & especially for success at Rotherfield FC that ultimately secured Wayne this opportunity. Wayne will be assisted by Alex Watts, to provide continuity following his appointment as first team assistant coach last season. The initial phase of pre-season will provide Wayne with the opportunity to assess the playing squad as he looks to use his serious coaching ability to improve player & ultimately team performance. He will also oversee coaching of all first team & reserves players.  After the upward trajectory of performance in the last 3 seasons under the careful guidance of Andy Garrett this is now an exciting time for the club to really kick on to build upon excellent foundations. Welcome Clarkey to the wonderful family that is Rotherfield Football Club!

Plain Content: September is around the corner which means that the football season is almost upon us! Ok, well for some its started and some of our age groups have been doing some pre-season sessions and friendlies already. However Saturday 7th September is when football sessions for our Foundation Phase age groups (primary school years) starts at Rotherfield Recreation Ground. The club is excited to welcome both current and new players to the club and we hope you enjoy the coming season. Below are the Saturday morning session times for the season: U6s 9.30 - 10.15am U7s 9.00 - 10.00am U8s 9.00 - 10.00am U9s 10.30 - 11.30am U10s 10.30 - 11.30am Don't forget to pop into our clubhouse and visit 4Ds Snack Bar where you can get a cuppa and a snack while enjoying your young ones play. But that's not all, 7/8th September is also the inaugural weekend of the C&DJFL 2024/25 season with our U11 Red Star traveling to Uckfield Grasshoppers Raiders on the Saturday. On the Sunday, our U12 Rebels are also away to Uckfield Grasshoppers Rhinos, while the U12 Rovers welcome Tonbridge Invicta Spitfires. The U13 Raptors entertain Uckfield Grasshoppers Hornets. Our 16s have an exciting trip to the home of Tonbridge Angels, THE HALCYON WEALTH LONGMEAD STADIUM, to face Tonbridge Junior Town.  Lastly, our U17s are also in Tonbridge and face Tonbridge Junior Thistle. However the most exciting news is to come. This season we were delighted to have our first ever all girls team which will compete in the U12 Girls division.  They have their first game on Saturday morning against East Grinstead Meads Girls Real. Also Friday 6th September sees the return of our Wildcats group at Rotherfield Recreation Ground starting at 5.30pm. To follow our Junior teams progress in full visit FA Full Time Crowborough & Junior District League and select the division you want to view.

Plain Content: This weekend, Rotherfield FC remembered those fallen in conflict. Over the weekend all players paused for a moment to reflect and respect those who gave the ultimate sacrifice in war. Rotherfield Sports Club Secretary Elliot Ridley-Smith attended the annual service of remembrance on the Ashdown Forest Airman's Grave on behalf of the club. Thousands of people come to the service on a site where a Wellington bomber crash landed returning from Germany and killing all 6 young young men on board, the eldest only 27 years old. Elliot laid a poppy wreath at the site, along with a number of local organisations, on behalf of Rotherfield Sports Club. Rotherfield FC has also lost members in war, most notably the Green Boys who played for Rotherfield pre 1st World War but most did not return.

Plain Content: Image: Andrew Hazelden Final Score: 15–0  Venue: Fortress Rotherfield  Date: A gloriously September afternoon Rotherfield Vets kicked off their home campaign in style — well, eventually — against Diversity United Vets, on a pitch so lush it could’ve hosted a David Attenborough documentary. The recent rains had done wonders, and so had the squad list: a whopping 24 players available, which is either a manager’s dream or a logistical nightmare. Manager McInnes, ever the diplomat, gave minutes to those yet to feature this season. In came John Penny, Seb Chick, Wayne Robshaw (who’d already played that morning in Lancing), and Paul Barnes, who jetted in from Paris with international clearance in hand. Très bien. As the lads limbered up under Garrett’s famously vigorous warm-up routine, one question loomed: where on earth were Diversity United? McInnes tried calling every number on their team sheet. No luck. Then, at 13:44, a single car rolled in with five bewildered opposition players. Cue frantic checks of the welcome letter — yes, correct postcode, yes, correct kick-off time, yes, it was indeed an 11-a-side match. Eventually, enough players trickled in to start the game, with Diversity fielding nine men and one more en route (and soon leave again after being sin-binned). Despite the chaos, Rotherfield were in no mood to be complacent. Penny set the tone early by somehow ballooning over the bar from point-blank range—perhaps aiming for the moon? The breakthrough came on 14 minutes: DT latched onto a Garrett through-ball and slotted home. Ten minutes later, Garrett turned provider again, this time for Alex Thompson, who made it 2–0. The floodgates opened. Goals from Wilkins, Brooker (x2), Seb Chick, and Taylor saw the Greens cruise into halftime at 7–0. The second half saw the bench emptied: Brunger, Barnes, Watson, Burton, and Cullum all joined the fray. Taylor and Brooker, both stuck on two goals, were visibly twitchy. Clibbens, meanwhile, was lobbying hard to play up front, worried his top scorer crown was under siege. The Greens didn’t let up. Penny nodded in the easiest of headers, and Clibbens made a 100-metre dash from centre-back when a penalty was awarded to bury his third of the season—Usain Bolt would’ve been proud. Taylor and Brooker returned with vengeance, combining beautifully to torment the now-exhausted defence. Taylor bagged a second-half hat-trick (five goals total), Brooker completed his own treble, and Cullum, Wilkins, and Barnes added to the tally. Final score: 15–0. Yes, you read that right. That’s as many goals as Rotherfield scored in the entirety of last season. A strange game, but a memorable one. Next up: the short trip up the B2100 to Jarvis Brook on 5th October for what’s being dubbed the Vets’ El Clásico. Bring popcorn. 🧑‍💼 Squad List Starters: W. Robshaw, A. Garrett, C. King, M. Plain Content: A first meeting of this season between the two teams promoted last season, ended in a familiar draw. However the story of this game revolved around two absolute Worldy strikes from distance, a 3G pitch surface that was as unkempt as it possibly could be & a gale force wind that buffeted ears all game. With a squad ravaged by illness, injuries & unavailability it was important that Rotherfield started well in a compact shape. The perfect start arrived when Lewis “raging bull” Bowen turned & let fly from 25 yards (22m for those who are younger than this reporter) with the ball arriving into the top corner after 4 minutes. Both sides sparred but the loss of Charlie Cosser after only 10 minutes to an impact related knee injury from the unforgiving pitch meant a further reshuffle of resources for the visitors. 5 minutes later & the home side restored parity with a half volley strike from 30 yards (27m!) into the top corner. Young Oscar then entered the match to make his debut in adult football when Connor Evans had to be withdrawn with another impact injury. The work rate of the visitors players was highly commendable with the defence of King, Bowen, Ridley & Sutton needing to be on full alert given the possession percentage of Eastbourne. All square at half time. The second half was very similar to the first with the wind being the most influential player! The home side slowly took control of the match with some attacking substitutions to increase their threat but the level of resolution of Rotherfield was now turned up to max. Owen Ridley was very assured, surprising given his holiday of the last couple of weeks, Will Sutton was never beaten by his man, Craig King was solid offering a calm way out in possession whilst the raging bull was at his physical best showing a love of defending usually missing in centre forwards. One (of many) defensive header from Bowen was sensational. In front of the defence the work rate of skipper Rich Holman & James Dunn was a joy to behold whilst young Jacob & Oskar Furman on the other side of midfield ran, ran, tackled, challenged & then ran some more. The vets legend that is Fothers was also not shy of a challenge whilst trying gainfully to provide an attacking threat but a diet of morsels was not conducive to feeding threat. Goalkeeper Kieran Sumner was a calm presence at the back always trying to build possession, with sensible instructive chat to those in front of him. With 10 minutes remaining it was Sumner who saved brilliantly low to his right to deflect at full stretch a goal bound shot out for a corner. In the time that remained the wind increased in strength & then the appalling pitch claimed another victim when Evans slipped on the tarmac surround just beyond the goal line to significantly graze a knee that resulted in his removal from the fray. A very significant away point earned by a performance that characterised the strength of Rotherfield FC in that ego’s are left at home whilst everyone gives absolutely everything to try to get something from every game following implicitly the instructions from new manager James Bowen. Squad: Sumner, King, Ridley, Cosser, Sutton, Jacob, Holman (c), Dunn, Evans, Fothergill, Bowen Subs used Furman, Oscar

Image Credit: Will Hugall On Saturday, our Firsts welcome Hailsham Town FC to the Recreation Ground in the third round of the Sussex County FA Intermediate Cup. A win for Rotherfield will secure them a home fixture in the Quarter Finals. Sam Saunders and co. will be eager to get on the front foot early to get back to the stellar level of performance as demonstrated in the 4-2 home win against Frenches Athletic. Fan favourites Jack Turner, Max Carbune, Mike Peevor and Callum Ridley are likely to feature as well as Rotherfield Junior alumni Archie Russell and Kieran Sumner. Archie and Kieran both played as Juniors at the club since the age of 4 with Archie now cementing himself as a first team player and Kieran breaking in to the side recently having proved himself in the Reserves. Dan Gray will be looking to add to his goal tally as after his quick brace and inspired performance last week earning the Greens a valuable point. Jack Spampanato will also be hunting for goals as he and Gray are joint top scorers so there may be competition between them to edge ahead! Join us tomorrow afternoon which promises to be a great display of local league football. Fixture: Rotherfield vs Hailsham Town Competition: Sussex County FA Intermediate Cup - Third Round Venue: Rotherfield Recreation Ground, North Street, TN6 3LX KO: 2pm Referee: Nick Heater Refreshments available at half time, bar open at full time. Please note, no dogs are allowed at the Recreation Ground.

Plain Content: Cup Tie – Pease Pottage The Rotherfield Vets rolled into Pease Pottage for their third game in four weeks with the smallest squad of the season for their SSFL Vets Cup (In memory of Ian Dean). Brooker and Harkness answered the late SOS call, proving that sometimes heroes don’t wear capes — they just remember where they left their shin pads. Despite the lean numbers, the Greens put in a quality performance and marched into the next round of the cup. First Half The Greens came out flying and really should have been two goals up before Furngate nicked the opener. A long punt upfield caught the defence napping, the sun blinded Robshaw, and the Furngate striker skipped through to slot into an empty net. (Note to self: sunglasses might be added to the kit list next week.) Furngate stuck to their “kick it long and hope for the best” tactic, but Rotherfield began to bite back. Brooker and Hodges were causing chaos down the wings, while Cullum, Mansford, and Penny closed down the midfield like bouncers outside a nightclub. Clibbens thought he’d equalised with a towering header, only for the linesman to raise his flag — presumably for crimes against gravity. Moments later, Cullum somehow managed to head over the bar from two yards out, proving that even miracles have limits. Thankfully, Hodges — in only his second vets game — curled in a beauty to make it 1-1. His first goal for the club, and judging by his celebration, you’d think he’d just won the World Cup. Rotherfield then took the lead before halftime. A slick counterattack saw Hodges streak through one-on-one and calmly chip the keeper. 1-2 to the Greens at the break, and Riley’s defence looked as solid as a pub dartboard on a Friday night. Second Half The restart couldn’t have gone better: within 30 seconds Brooker buried one to make it 1-3. Manager McInnes shuffled the pack, bringing on Ead, Brunger, Harkness, and Tsang, all of whom slotted in seamlessly — like IKEA furniture, but without the missing screws. From then on, it was one-way traffic. The Greens peppered the Furngate goal, and the game should have been put to bed long before Brooker chased down a loose ball, outpaced the keeper, and squared for Clibbens to tap into an empty net. 1-4, job done, and Furngate well and truly finished. Final Whistle A cracking performance from a small but mighty squad. The Greens advance to the next round, where Woodingdean await. Special shout-out to Hodges — two goals in only his second vets game. At this rate, he’ll be demanding his own chant by Christmas.

Plain Content: EMC Academy 1-1 Rotherfield FC Rotherfield FC earned their second, successive away draw this weekend as a competitive and high-quality affair against EMC Academy ended 1-1. A tale of two halves, Rotherfield went into a first-half lead thanks to Jack Spampanato and defended resolutely in the second period to earn another point. After months with no rain whatsoever, torrential rain greeted both sides during the warm up at AFC Whyteleafe where Rotherfield lined up with three changes from the week prior as Bailey Mintrim, Harry Chittenden and Callum Gallie took their places in the starting lineup. The early exchanges saw both sides cancelling each other out with few clear cut chances being generated. As the half progressed, the Greens began to enjoy more joy down the left hand side with Mintrim and Daniel Gray combining well. The midfield three of Jack Spampanato, John Sinclair and Chittenden were industrious out of possession and showing good quality on the ball as Rotherfield gained the upper hand. Their superiority and sustained pressure would tell after a well-delivered free kick from Spampanato was cleared to the edge of the box. Twenty yards from goal, Gray and Spampanato combined well and the Rotherfield #10 curled the ball into the far corner to give the visitors the lead. EMC rallied well after going behind and their pacy wide men were causing problems with the evergreen Sid Sollis dropping deep and getting on the ball. Rotherfield looked to have weathered the storm but were disappointed to concede right on the stroke of half time. EMC’s left winger cut inside and shot towards goal which looped over James Gurney into the back of the net. The hosts started the second half positively and the Greens had the strong defending of Gallie, Callum Ridley, James Bowen and Mintrim to thank as well as Gurney who clawed away a number of dangerous crosses. The pattern of the second half was set with EMC enjoying the majority of possession and Rotherfield looking to hit their hosts on the break. Despite a number of decent openings with dangerous runs from the likes of Cameron Howard and Gray as well as a long-range effort from Tommy Overton, the Greens were unable to test the home side’s keeper.  The home side continued to make changes and their pace from the bench was a real threat for Rotherfield to contend with. Changes were made by the away side to stem the flow and the Greens were showing real discipline in their shape and defending. As the clock ticked on, the hosts looked to have won the game with a far post header from a deep corner only for the officials to strike the goal out as the ball had gone out of play during the corner delivery. The final moments saw both sides pushing for a winner but the final whistle brought an end to an entertaining game from start to finish. Next week, Rotherfield continue their travels as they head to Cuckfield Town looking to get their first victory of the season. Plain Content: 26th April 2026 The B2100 Old Man’s El Clásico On a glorious Sunday afternoon, local rivals Jarvis Brook made the short pilgrimage down the B2100 to the Rotherfield recreation ground for what has become affectionately known as The Old Man’s El Clásico. Sunshine, a decent crowd, and two teams full of creaking joints — all that was missing was a comeback win that, after 37 minutes, looked wildly unlikely. Rotherfield actually started brightly. With returning skipper Riley marshalling the defence and Garrett organising absolutely everything else, the Greens kept the ball well and produced some neat build‑up play in the opening minutes. Then, with their first venture into our half in the 5th minute, Jarvis Brook somehow found themselves 0–1 up.  Football can be cruel! Still, heads stayed up and Rotherfield continued to play the better football, even if the final-third decisions occasionally resembled a raffle draw. With the heat rising, a drinks break arrived — along with the first rotation: Brooker for Oddy (who had taken the “run yourself into the ground” brief a little too literally), Hodges for Thompson, and DT for Alun. Despite the changes, Rotherfield kept control of the game… only to fall 0–2 behind from Jarvis Brook’s second meaningful attack, a corner where their height advantage did the damage. But this team doesn’t fold. Not anymore. Wilkins decided enough was enough, took the game by the scruff of the neck, and became borderline unplayable. His goal pulled Rotherfield back into it. Moments later, on the stroke of half-time, King — who had been marauding forward like a man who’d forgotten he was a defender — delivered a sumptuous back‑post corner. DT rose, guided his header back across the keeper, and found the top corner. 2–2, fully deserved. Half-Time: 2–2 McInnes and guest assistant Watts shuffled the pack again at the break, bringing back Evans, Oddy and Thompson. The football only improved. Thompson began pulling strings in midfield, Wilkins continued terrorising the Brook defence with his pace, and Hodges caused problems on the opposite flank. The pressure finally told around the hour mark: Oddy cut the ball back beautifully and Wilkins smashed home his second. 3–2 — the comeback complete. Mansford made way for Matt Moore, who brought his usual calmness to the final half-hour. Another drinks break followed, with McGuire returning for Riley, Ashton replacing King, Brooker for Oddy, and DT for Evans. For those who’ve watched the Vets this season, a late lead is usually a source of mild panic. But not today. Instead, fans were treated to the pirouettes, spins and drag-backs of centre-back Seb Chick, who embarked on an unexpected forward run that will live long in the memory. The game was sealed when Thompson put the icing on the cake, smashing home Rotherfield’s fourth past the helpless keeper. Full-Time: Rotherfield Vets 4–2 Jarvis Brook Vets A brilliant way to end the season — arguably the best all‑round team performance of the campaign, with all 16 players contributing superbly. As the season closes, we’ll reflect on the good, the bad, and the occasionally very ugly… and then go again. If you’re reading this and fancy joining the squad next season, get in touch. Starters: M. Plain Content: Rotherfield FC made it back to back wins in the Gray Hooper Holt LLP Mid Sussex Premier Division thanks to a comfortable 5-0 victory on their travels away to Polegate Town. Goals from Harry Brand, Scott Taylor, Sam Saunders, Bailey Mintrim and Jack Turner gave the Greens a dominant away victory, climbing a place in the table as they did so. Arriving at The Trafalgar Ground, home of Newhaven Town, for yesterday’s fixture fresh off the back of a good away victory at Cuckfield Rangers the week prior, the Greens were forced to shuffle their pack due to absentees and injuries. The lineup saw Harry Brand make his first start for the club after impressing last week on debut off the bench and Jack Draper make his first appearance for the first team after graduating from Rotherfield’s youth setup. The early exchanges between both sides lacked any sort of flow as possession turned over routinely between both sides. A couple of deep crosses from wide for Polegate Town looked to cause concern for the away side’s defence and a goal was chalked off for a foul in the box - a sigh of relief for the Greens. As the first half progressed, the Greens managed to create more openings and take more control of the game. The close control and forward running of Jack Spampanato impressing in his midfield role and with Brand looking a sustained threat cutting in from the left showing excellent movement. After going close a couple of times it was Brand who would take the deadlock with a fantastic looping shot on the angle finding the back of the net to give the visitors the lead. Despite not clicking into top gear, Rotherfield managed the game to half time with their slender lead in place. At the interval, the away side’s management called for greater composure on the ball and patience in waiting for the right opportunities. The introductions of skipper Sam Saunders and Scott Taylor, both on their return from injury, afforded the away side greater control and creativity in possession and their impact was in full force soon. A long free-kick was excellently controlled by the ever-industrious Mike Peevor who beat his marker and squared for Taylor to find the bottom corner from the edge of the area to double the Greens’ lead. Two became three soon after as Spampanato was felled on the edge of the area and captain Saunders stepped up to curl a fantastic strike over the wall and into the top corner. The Greens were in full flow now with the powerful running of Dan Gray, Connor Morrow and Bailey Mintrim looking a real threat with every attacking move. The fourth goal game in more fortuitous fashion as a Polegate defender attempted to clear a deep cross, only for his clearance to cannon back off of the ever-willing Mintrim and into the back of the net. The final goal came from another Saunders free-kick who forced the Polegate keeper into action only for Jack Turner to power the follow-up home from close range to round off the scoring. Back-to-back wins for the Greens but also impressively, the result represented back-to-back clean sheets for Rotherfield with yesterday’s performance built on the solidity of a changed back four of Richard Holman, Max Carbune, Turner and Mintrim who defended admirably throughout and the safe hands of James Gurney. The afternoon was topped off with a solid display from young defender Jack Draper who enjoyed fifteen minutes at full-back to mark his debut for the first team, making a strong shot-bound block in the process. The Greens continue their succession of away travels next week as they head to Frenches Athletic looking to make it three wins on the bounce. Lineup: Gurney; Holman, Carbune, Turner, Mintrim; Chittenden (Saunders, 50), Peevor, Spampanato (Draper, 75); Howard (Taylor, 60), Morrow, Brand (Gray, 50)

Plain Content: Rotherfield Reserves maintained their good start to life in Division 2 South with a convincing win against the student medics. On a lovely afternoon & with a pristine pitch it was a surprise when it was the young medics that started the quicker especially given they had a minimal warm up after a late arrival, with their kit the latest of all. A one nil lead after 10 minutes for the visitors ensued. However the home side grew into the game, scoring a quick equaliser & then marching into a 4-1 half time lead with some top quality goals (2 from Lewis Bowen, 1 for Harry McInulty & 1 for young Jacob). The second half saw Rotherfield get better especially in their defensive shape with skipper Rich Holman & Jack Birdsall anchoring the midfield superbly to take the pressure off the defence. This allowed full backs Archie Russell (back from his European Grand tour) & Will Sutton to show their quality, & it was a surprise that only one more goal was added with Bowen completing an excellent hat trick. A strong three points to build confidence even with a large number of players not available. Squad: Sumner, Russel l, Sutton, Cosser, King, Holman (c), Birdsall, Bristow, McInulty, Evans, Bowen. Subs used: Jacob, Furman Player of match Lewis Bowen.

Plain Content: Captain Sam Saunders was awarded Man of the Match on Saturday. Image credit Will Hugall. Rotherfield FC returned to winning ways this weekend with a resounding away victory against Punnetts Town. Goals from Mike Peevor, George Fyffe, James Dunn and Jack Turner rewarded the Green and Whites with a much-needed three points.   The side made the short journey to Punnetts Town in determined mood, looking to bounce back after a disappointing home defeat to Cuckfield Rangers last time out. Rotherfield were buoyed by the returns of Callum Ridley, John Sinclair, George Fyffe and Sam Saunders and started the game in strong fashion. The new attacking trio of Peevor, Fyffe and Jack Spampanato looked dangerous in the early exchanges, with James Dunn providing a probing threat from midfield.   The deadlock was broken inside fifteen minutes with Peevor, restored to the number nine position, scoring a trademark backwards header from an expert Ridley cross after a well-worked throw on the left-hand side.   Spampanato continued to cause problems for the home side’s defence and, having found space in front of the back four, released Cameron Routledge out wide to find George Fyffe inside the box, who powered home a thunderous strike.   The home side were not without their chances, and a great delivery and header from a corner forced Kieran Sumner into a strong point-blank save. That said, it was the Greens who were enjoying the majority of the play and would make it three-nil before half-time. A customary late run into the box from Dunn saw him gamble at the back post and get to the ball first before the onrushing keeper.   In poor weather and with a difficult surface, the call at half-time was for sensible heads defensively and even more intent in the opposition’s half. The Greens picked up where they left off with good chances falling to Peevor, Fyffe and Spampanato but they found the Punnetts Town goalkeeper in good form.   The fourth goal would come, however, owing to another excellent set-piece delivery from Saunders, whose corner was met powerfully by Turner to head home and extend the away side’s lead. A fifth almost soon followed with Dunn and Routledge combining excellently down the right, leading Routledge to unleash a ferocious shot which cannoned back off the crossbar.   Changes followed as Gaffer, Wayne Clarke, took the opportunity to get some rest into the legs of Sinclair, Turner, Ridley and Peevor with the youthful legs of Gray, Prince and Russell impressing as they emerged from the bench.   In truth, Punnetts Town’s best spell of the game came in the closing exchanges but a combination of good handling from Sumner and the highest of standards from skipper Saunders in midfield ensured Rotherfield collected their first clean sheet of the season and a well-deserved three points. Plain Content: Image: Will Hugall 📰 SSFL Vets Division 2 – Sunday 7th September 2025 Venue: Somewhere under Gatwick’s flight path Fulltime: 1 -2 After a summer of rigorous pre-season prep (read: two friendlies and a lot of WhatsApp banter), Rotherfield Vets launched their 2025-26 campaign with an away day against Horsham Crusaders. The squad was stacked… with defenders. So stacked, in fact, that the GOAT himself had to don the gloves and play in goal. Tactical genius or sheer chaos? You decide. The first half was a scrappy affair, with both teams struggling to tame a pitch that looked like it had been trimmed by a blind sheep. Horsham nearly took the lead early on, but their striker’s tap-in attempt was sabotaged by a rogue bobble and the crossbar – a combo more brutal than a VAR decision. Rotherfield began to find joy down the wings, with Craig King (in his 400th appearance – someone get this man a testimonial and a statue) linking up nicely with Ben Brooker. Despite the pressure, the breakthrough eluded them. Instead, they earned a new nickname: Long-Ball Merchants. Charming! Horsham eventually broke the deadlock after a midfield mishap gifted their striker a clean run at goal. He finished with style, and the hosts went into halftime 1 -0 up. Halftime: 1 -0 Cue the halftime team talk: calm, constructive, and only mildly sarcastic. Whatever was said worked, because Rotherfield came out flying. A delicious free-kick from Alex Thompson found Richard Clibbens lurking at the back post, who nodded home like a man who’s done it a thousand times. 1 -1. Moments later, Clibbens was rugby tackled in the box. Penalty! After a brief game of “You take it” – “No, you take it” – Clibbens stepped up and slotted it home. 2 -1. Comeback complete. The next 20 minutes saw Rotherfield dominate, with fresh legs from the bench making an impact. Ashton, Watson, and Fuller all came on, with Fuller immediately causing chaos. A robust challenge sparked a minor diplomatic incident, with the opposition bench calling for sanctions and the referee doing his best impersonation of a UN peacekeeper. Rotherfield were now not just long-ball merchants – they were thugs. Progress? The final minutes brought drama. Horsham’s striker unleashed a rocket destined for the top corner, but Andy Garrett, channelling his inner Buffon, pulled off a worldie save to tip it over the bar. That was the moment. That was the win. ⭐ Final Whistle Thoughts First win of the season ✅ First ever SSFL win ✅ Called long-ball merchants AND thugs ✅✅ Craig King’s 400th game 🎉 Garrett’s save worthy of a mural 🧤 A solid performance, a gritty win, and a perfect launchpad for the season ahead. 🧑‍💼 Squad List Starting: A. Plain Content: Wow! What a goal fest. With the first team game postponed owing to a waterlogged pitch at Shoreham the watching clubmen were treated to a thriller on a pitch that was remarkably good given 60mm of rain in the week albeit it was soft in a few places. The first minute saw Scotty Taylor go down in the visitors penalty area after a clumsy challenge but the appeals were waved away by the official. Ringmer should have opened the scoring after some calamitous home defending but somehow Will Sutton blocked the final shot with his face whilst lying prone on the line. Skipper Owen Ridley then determinedly blocked two shots when a goal seemed inevitable before the home side took the lead. Taylor received the ball in a wide left position before playing a quality pass into the run of Ridley who steered the ball superbly into the net. However ten minutes later & Ringmer equalised after more shoddy defending. Back came the greens & the lively Ryan Blackstone was through on goal only for the keeper to save, Sean Bristow shot tamely when in a good position following good work from the industrious Jack Birdsall, & Taylor shot over when the opportunity created deserved better. Then on the stroke of half time left back Will Sutton fired into the top corner from a wide position when a cross would have been more typical! It was a cross, surely? The second half was even more of a roller coaster ride but the first meaningful action saw Ringmer equalise from a corner. The ball was allowed to bounce in the six yard box as no one showed any leadership & inevitably the ball was headed into the net. Rotherfield piled forward yet again with a Blackstone header flashing just wide after a quality cross from the right by Lloyd Brazier & Jacob started to influence the attacking play on the left but his shot was fired over. Then Blackstone again found space in behind the visiting defence & when he went around the keeper this time he was unceremoniously flattened by a crude challenge. Penalty awarded & a deserved yellow card for the Ringmer keeper. Taylor despatched a quality penalty for Rotherfield to take the lead again. It was the turn of Ringmer to flood forward now & with the home defence looking shaky at best it was not a surprise to see Ringmer equalise (again) seizing on an opportunity following an inability to clear the ball effectively. Then as the home side over committed going forward Ringmer exploited the space to take the lead for the first time. The game now entered the final 10 minutes with Rotherfield showing loads of character, grunt & effort but quality & composure were lacking. Repeatedly chances did not result after good approach play & a desire to get the ball forward too quickly just gave it back to Ringmer. Then in the 98th minute it was Taylor who scored after playing an excellent give & go with Birdsall, salvaging a point with a quality moment. This was a hugely entertaining game & the 3 young teenagers in the home starting line up will have learned a lot as they continue their exposure to adult football. Well done to Sam, Jack & Jacob. Plain Content: Balcombe emerged victorious in an entertaining contest against Rotherfield in the Gray Hooper Holt LLP Mid Sussex Football League Premier Division, running out 4–2 winners at Warden Park Academy 3G. Balcombe made the brighter start and took the lead through Marco Jota, whose mishit cross deceived James Gurney and sailed over the goalkeeper into the net to give the hosts the advantage. Rotherfield responded swiftly. A long throw from Mike Hodges caused problems in the Balcombe penalty area, evading everyone including the home keeper, who was unable to gather cleanly as the ball crept over the line for the equaliser. The Greens grew in confidence and soon turned the game around. With Balcombe struggling to deal with a loose ball in the box, Bailey Mintrim produced a pinpoint finish to make it 2–1 to Rotherfield just before half-time. Balcombe returned after the break with renewed intent, but Rotherfield defended resolutely for the opening 20 minutes of the second half. However, the hosts found a way back into the game when a long throw of their own was launched into the area, sailed over the defence, and was nodded home to restore parity. With around 20 minutes remaining, Dan Gray was introduced and quickly made his presence felt. Latching onto a long forward ball, his pace carried him beyond a defence that appeared to be anticipating an offside flag. One-on-one with the keeper, his effort struck the far post. Moments later, Balcombe broke swiftly and capitalised, taking the lead once more. Rotherfield reshuffled, introducing Owen Ridley and pushing Callum Ridley further forward in search of an equaliser. The move almost paid dividends when substitute Will Sutton delivered a deep cross that fell invitingly to Callum Ridley. He connected well on the half-volley, but his effort lacked power and drifted narrowly off target. As Rotherfield pushed late on, Balcombe sealed the result near the end with a rifled strike from inside the box to make it 4–2 and put the contest beyond doubt.

Plain Content: Rotherfield Show Resilience in 2–2 Draw at Hollington United Rotherfield FC produced a spirited performance to earn a hard-fought 2–2 draw away at Hollington United in the Gray Hooper Holt LLP Mid-Sussex Football League Premier Division on Saturday 17 January 2026. The match also saw goalkeeper James Gurney make his return to First Team football following a shoulder injury, while Phil Teague came into the side in the absence of Jack Turner. The opening stages saw the ball spend plenty of time in the air at the Rise Electrical Gibbons Memorial Ground, with both sides adapting to a heavy playing surface made difficult by the week’s persistent rain. Clear chances were at a premium in a competitive first half, and neither team was able to gain a decisive foothold as the sides went into the break level at 0–0. Hollington broke the deadlock early in the second half when a dangerous ball was played across goal and tapped in at the far post. Rotherfield responded impressively and were soon back on level terms, Phil Teague marking his return to the starting XI in style by showing great composure to slot home after meeting a well-delivered free kick from wide. Buoyed by the equaliser, the Greens continued to press and were rewarded with a superb second goal as John Sinclair connected sweetly with a half-volley to put Rotherfield ahead. With momentum on their side, Rotherfield looked capable of seeing the game out, but with just over ten minutes remaining the hosts restored parity, finding the net despite James Gurney getting a hand to the effort. Both sides pushed for a winner in the closing stages, but neither could find a decisive breakthrough, and the points were ultimately shared after an entertaining contest. Man of the Match: James Gurney 🧤

Plain Content: Rotherfield Sign Off Season with Composed Win Over Reigate Priory Rotherfield rounded off their Mid Sussex Football League Premier Division campaign with a controlled and disciplined performance in warm conditions, securing a deserved victory over Reigate Priory. The hosts made a bright start and wasted little time asserting themselves. Just five minutes in, Connor Morrow showcased his quality, keeping possession well before unleashing an audacious effort from outside the area that looped over the goalkeeper to open the scoring. Morrow remained at the heart of everything positive, and only two minutes later he was involved again—this time nodding the ball into the path of Sincs, who drove forward with intent and calmly dispatched his finish beyond the keeper to double the lead inside seven minutes. Rotherfield continued to press, with Morrow again threatening midway through the half, breaking through and forcing a strong save from the Reigate keeper. From the resulting pressure, a corner was delivered shortly after, falling to Jack Turner, whose volley unfortunately sailed over the bar. The third goal came in the 25th minute following a well-worked move. Dan Gray delivered an inviting cross from the left, which Sincs controlled expertly on his chest before being shoved in the back—leaving the referee with no hesitation in pointing to the spot. Sam Saunders stepped up confidently and converted to extend Rotherfield’s advantage. The second half proved to be a more scrappy and hot-tempered affair, with fewer clear-cut chances as both sides battled the heat and rising tensions. Despite this, Rotherfield still looked the more dangerous side. Around the 75-minute mark, a flurry of attacking intent saw Dan Gray, Oscar Furman, and Sean Bristow all go close in quick succession, each denied as they searched to add a fourth. Reigate Priory’s best opportunity came late on, forcing Gurney into a strong save to maintain the clean sheet. Moments before full time, the visitors had one final chance on the break but dragged their effort wide, summing up a frustrating afternoon for them. In the end, it was a professional and composed display from Rotherfield, capping off their season on a high note with a well-earned win.

Plain Content: In their first pre-season friendly, the Reserves were good value for a stalemate at Wadhurst. Dominating for much of the first half while playing uphill — and what a hill it was — Rotherfield created a number of opportunities. Xander Hamza shot tamely after some good approach play, before Harry Chittenden failed to test the home keeper following an excellent passing move, although it was with his left foot! With James Bowen and Owen Ridley forming an impressive central defensive partnership, the home side were kept well away from Alfie Jukes, making his debut in the Rotherfield goal. The second half saw Wadhurst come more into the game, as they also found it easier playing up the slope. Jukes was called upon to tip a routine effort over the bar before producing a good save low to his left, securing the ball at the second attempt. With seven substitutes and a plethora of positional changes, it was inevitable that the second half became somewhat staccato. However, by the final whistle, debuts had been made, match fitness had been boosted and every player had contributed positively to a decent run-out. A useful first outing for the Reserves as preparations for the new season continue. Rotherfield Reserves Squad: Jukes, Sellings, J Bowen, L Bowen, Sutton, Gabriel S, Gabriel B, Ridley O, Chittenden, Birdsall, Dunn, Alexander, Hamza, Peevor, Bristow, Brazier, Furman, Wilson.

Plain Content: Friday 8th May, Rotherfield Football Club hosted the annual Awards Night. Dan Taylor was BBQ chef for the evening and Stuart McInnes and Andy Garrett set up the 4 -a-side footgolf tournament., with the winning side featuring Jack Turner, Nathan Milroy, Sam Saunders and Richard Clibbens (below) Club Chairman Pete Ford opened the formal proceedings thanking everyone who had made this season possible. Young Player Of The Year Archie Russell receiving the Josh Alexander #21 Award being presented by Pete Ford for his consistent performances in the First Team. The 'Significant Goal' Award in memory of Aaron King being presented to Jack Birdsall. This was presented in recognition of his first senior goal at the club against Southwick which then cemented his place in the Reserve team. Veterans Joint Players' Player of the Season Richard Clibbens, being presented his award by Veterans Chairman Stuart 'Jocky' McInnes Reserve Team Manager's Player Of The Year was awarded to James Bowen. Reserve Team Players' Player of the Year went to Seb Chick. First Team Manager's Player of the Year and Players' Player of the Year went to John Sinclair. Clubperson of the Year was awarded to Dilan Nlendi for his commitment to playing and training. For a full review of Rotherfield FC's season, you can download the Club Newsletter below.

Plain Content: Our club Quiz night on 18th October has been cancelled as a consequence of a lack of entered teams. This is very disappointing given the work to plan such an event: booking the hall, applying for a licence, securing raffle prizes, purchasing bar stock, writing the quiz etc. We have wasted some money but minimised our losses by acting swiftly. Previous quiz nights raised £1000+ & this year the fund raising was for indoor training for our junior squads. Why did only 5 teams enter? The previous quiz had over 20 teams and was a great success and many said how enjoyable the night was. Was it the time of year? Was it the cost? Was it because a quiz night is not appealing? We have always tried to keep our junior fees as low as possible to ensure we are inclusive. We don’t waste your money on nice to have team wear, or bags but there are lots of costs for football that are increasing. If our fundraising events are not supported then the club may have to consider increasing fees to fund junior football. We don't want to do that so please let us know why you didn’t support the quiz or better still what you would support & how you are prepared to help organise. Please use the link attached to leave an anonymous response. Please don’t leave responding to others, let us know! https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1ClbV4ud8LbVysM2Ha-FC0QfTMDCF0rFR7rR-ystKK-s/edit?chromeless=1

Plain Content: Image: Will Hugall Rotherfield were on the receiving end of a 0-3 defeat this afternoon at the Recreation Ground. Both sides had opportunities to take the lead early but either fortuitous defending or poor finishing kept the score line 0 - 0 for the first half an hour of the contest. It was on the half hour mark, that John Sinclair conceded a freekick on the edge of the box. The free kick took a deflection off the defensive wall and keeper James Gurney was unable to stop the ball finishing in the net.  0-1 to Hollington That's how it remained at the break. Rotherfield started the second half with intent especially when Connor Morrow received the ball 10 minutes after the restart and travelled towards the visitors goal to see his effort hit the bottom of the post. Around the 65 minute mark, Hollington were awarded a throw, which was launched into the mix to eventually be nodded into the net. 0 - 2. Not long after, Hollington were first to the ball from a Gurney goal kick. The ball fell in between both centre backs for the Hollington forward to slot his effort past Gurney. 0 - 3. Plain Content: Image credit: Will Hugall Rotherfield were eager to bounce back from last Saturday's result against Westfield with another home fixture, as we welcomed bottom of the league Shoreham. The visitors arrived to the Recreation Ground with no points on the board, so they had a point to prove against a side who had won three out of the last four fixtures. However, the first half, in particular, was a lacklustre performance with little threat from both sides. The Greens did retain the ball, but the final service wasn't there. It was 35 minutes in when the deadlock broke when a Greens final ball was picked up by the hosts and a Shoreham forward drove forward and finished passed, keeper Kieran Sumner. 0-1 down at the break but all was not lost. The Greens made three changes soon after the restart with Saunders, Zimmerman and Gray entering the fray. 55 minutes in and Gray was able to advance forward and restore parity with a calm finish past the Shoreham keeper. However, parity was short lived as Shoreham took the lead with an effort that was heading for Sumner's gloves but took a wicked deflection off of Carbune to end up in the net. It was Gray who saved the day again, with another finish with aplomb to make it 2-2. Rotherfield dominated possession for the reminder of the half and as the dark clouds rolled in and a heavy shower drenched all involved, Rotherfield were awarded a free kick in a dangerous position. Jack Spampanato stepped up to deliver over the wall and Callum Ridley, tapped home what was thought to be the winner, only to be deemed offside by the officials. Final Score 2-2 Squad: Sumner, Kerslake, Turner, Carbune, Russell, Ridley, Peevor, Milroy, Fyffe, Spampanato, Kent Subs: Clarke, Zimmerman, Gray, Saunders, Watts (unused) Man Of The Match: Dan Gray - only played 15 minutes but saved Rotherfield from a banana skin defeat with his two goals.

Plain Content: Grassroots football across England will take a quieter approach on the weekend of 14 and 15 March 2026 as clubs, leagues, parents and supporters take part in The FA’s Silent Support Weekend. The nationwide initiative encourages spectators to reduce sideline noise during youth matches, helping young players develop confidence, communicate with teammates and make their own decisions on the pitch. The goal is to create a calmer, more positive matchday environment where the focus remains firmly on the players and their enjoyment of the game. What Is Silent Support Weekend? Silent Support Weekend is designed to promote positive behaviour on the sidelines in grassroots youth football. Instead of shouting instructions or reacting vocally to the game, spectators are encouraged to support players through applause only, allowing the players’ voices to be heard on the pitch. The initiative helps reduce pressure and distraction for young players, enabling them to communicate more effectively with teammates and focus on learning and enjoying the game. Across the weekend, the key principles are simple: Spectators – Applause Only Coaches – Provide guidance when needed Players – Communicate, make decisions and play freely By reducing sideline noise, players have more space to develop their game, build confidence and enjoy a positive football experience. How Parents and Spectators Can Support the Initiative at Rotherfield Junior FC At Rotherfield Junior FC, parents and supporters play an important role in helping create a supportive and respectful matchday environment. Silent Support Weekend is an opportunity for everyone at the club to reinforce the values of grassroots football and put young players first. Here are some simple ways parents and spectators can support the initiative during fixtures. 1. Encourage Through Applause Spectators are encouraged to show support by clapping good play from both teams rather than shouting instructions or criticism from the sidelines. This creates a positive and respectful atmosphere while still showing appreciation for the players’ efforts. 2. Avoid Sideline Coaching One of the key principles of Silent Support Weekend is to allow coaches to lead communication during the game. Parents and spectators should avoid giving tactical instructions, allowing players to make decisions and learn from the game themselves. 3. Let the Players Solve Problems Football is an important learning environment for young people. A quieter sideline allows players to think, communicate and work together to solve problems on the pitch without conflicting messages from the sidelines. 4. Keep the Environment Positive Silent Support Weekend is about creating a supportive and enjoyable environment. Parents and spectators can help by remaining positive, showing respect to referees and players, and encouraging sportsmanship throughout the game. 5. Support All Players Applauding good play from both teams reinforces respect and fairness in grassroots football while helping young players enjoy the experience without unnecessary pressure. Why Silent Support Matters Feedback from previous Silent Support Weekends has shown that many young players enjoy the calmer atmosphere and feel more confident communicating with their teammates during games. By reducing sideline noise and pressure, the initiative helps young players: Develop confidence and independence Improve team communication Learn decision-making skills Enjoy the game in a positive environment Supporting Grassroots Football Together Silent Support Weekend is part of The FA’s wider commitment to improving behaviour across grassroots football and ensuring the game remains enjoyable, inclusive and respectful for young players. By embracing the initiative on 14 and 15 March 2026, everyone involved with Rotherfield Junior FC — players, coaches, parents and supporters — can help create a better matchday experience for young footballers. Sometimes the best support is simply letting the players play.
